findings.claim: On a collection page's list, with the tree setting off and the item pane kept for the visit after `?file=` is cleared, the tree button writes `tree:enabled:{drive}` on every press and cannot hide the pane.
findings.impact: After Play with the tree off, the user returns to the collection list (collection crumb or pane name) and presses the pane button to hide the pane. The press stores `true`. The next press stores `false`, and the visit immediately re-shows the pane. The pane never hides, and the stored tree setting changes for every later page of the drive. This happens silently in ordinary use.
findings.evidence: TwoPaneLayout.tsx:172-175 clears treeYieldStore (filePage=false) whenever no file is open. TwoPaneLayout.tsx:141-152, added by 16ac5adaf, keeps treeVisitStore active on the list through `visitUntilLeft && visitStarted.current`. useTreeVisible.ts:66 sends the press to the visit toggle only when `yieldState.filePage`. Otherwise useTreeVisible.ts:83-85 runs `setEnabled(!enabled)`, which writes storage. visible = visitVisible || … (useTreeVisible.ts:58-59) stays true. Once enabled is false again, TwoPaneLayout.tsx:143-152 calls show() again. TreeToggle.tsx:46 calls this toggle, and routeHidesTree does not hide the button on a collection route (driveViews.ts:74-91).
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Steps: tree:enabled:main=false, md+ width. Open /drive/main/collections/c1, press Play, then press the pane's collection name (?file= cleared, pane stays shown). Press the tree toggle: localStorage tree:enabled:main becomes 'true' and the pane stays. Press again: it becomes 'false', the visit re-shows, and the pane stays. Mutation check: the new test in CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx ('keeps the item pane when the collection name clears ?file=') never presses the toggle on the list and mocks TreeToggle to null, so it would not catch this.

bucket_proposal.reason: I13: hiding or re-showing a pane shown for the visit must not write tree:enabled:{drive}. I18 (revised SPEC-CORE-082 I8) requires such a pane to be hidden and re-shown by the button without writing storage.

findings.proposed_fix: Route the press to treeVisitStore.toggle whenever the visit is active, not only on a file page. For example, check `visit.active && besideViewport` before the `yieldState.filePage` branch.

findings.claim: The test added for the r7 F8 fix covers only the pane's visibility after `?file=` is cleared. No test covers the tree button on that list, and none covers the hidden state across that transition.
findings.impact: F1 passed the suite. The test file mocks TreeToggle to null (CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx), so no interaction with the kept visit is exercised.
findings.evidence: CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx mocks '@/components/TreeToggle' to `() => null`. TwoPaneLayout.queuePane.test.tsx exercises the toggle only with a file open (route params 'file=f1').
findings.repro: Mutation: delete the `visitUntilLeft` condition's interplay with useTreeVisible.toggle, or swap the branch order in useTreeVisible.toggle. No existing test changes outcome.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a case to TwoPaneLayout.queuePane.test.tsx that renders with `visitUntilLeft`, opens a file, clears it, presses the toggle and asserts that localStorage is untouched and the pane hides.

specification_compliance: r7 F7 (I28): fixed. FileDetailChrome.tsx replaces the trail only when `queuePage.replacesTrail`. FolderQueueHost sets it false and CollectionDetail sets it true. FileDetailChrome.test.tsx covers both cases at wide and narrow widths.

r7 F8 (I19): fixed for visibility. TwoPaneLayout keeps the visit while `visitUntilLeft` is set and the pathname is unchanged, and clears it on a route change or unmount. The same fix introduces F1, which breaks I13/I18 on the list.
r7 F3: fixed. extraRowWidth counts the sidebar padding only when `leftPane.sidebarOverlay` (treeBeside || yielded). TreeYield.test.tsx adds the tree-off, sidebar-inline case and expects 'stacked'.
r7 unspecified index 2 (I11): fixed. CollectionItemsPane always receives `onSelect={playFile}`, so a first row choice requests play. A test was added.
I5/I6/I2/I3/I10 paths were not changed by these fix commits.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: On a collection page with the tree setting off, opening any file (a grid card or a link, not only Play or a row) starts the visit, and the item pane then stays shown on the collection list until the page is left.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: `visitStarted` is set by any `queuePane && hasFile`, so a card click with the tree off leaves the pane on the list afterwards.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Ending a folder queue (×, a choice outside the queue, or clearFile) removes `sort` and `order` even when they were the listing's own URL sort.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: The user sorts by URL, plays, and closes the queue. The listing falls back to its stored sort.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A play intent left pending by a selection that the navigation guard cancelled is consumed by the next arrival at that file by any route, which then autoplays.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: playIntent.ts holds the id until takePlayIntent matches it.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A visit-shown pane that the reader hid comes back after the viewport crosses md and returns, because the visit is cleared below md and shown again above it.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: TwoPaneLayout clears the visit when besideViewport is false and calls show() again with hidden=false.

regression_risks: useTreeVisible.toggle now meets an active visit with filePage=false on the collection list (F1).
TwoPaneLayout's visit effect depends on pathname refs. A pathname change that keeps the same TwoPaneLayout instance (collection → another collection) resets the visit, which is intended but untested.
FolderQueueHost still computes `name`/`href` for QueuePageState, but the trail no longer reads them. Only the pane uses them.
test_coverage: FileDetailChrome.test.tsx covers replacesTrail true and false, including the narrow back link.
TreeYield.test.tsx covers the inline sidebar with the tree off (stacked form, no storage write).
CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx covers the pane kept after ?file= is cleared and cleared on leaving, and a first row choice that autoplays.
No test presses the tree toggle on a collection list with a kept visit (F1/F2).
No e2e covers the kept visit. The queuePage fixture builds its own QueuePageState rather than using CollectionDetail.

I did not read AppShell or SidebarProvider to confirm the timing of the padding transition for the sidebarOverlay fix.
I did not re-read ShellLayout, MarkdownDocumentLayout, RightPaneFile or the players beyond the diff for this round.
I did not verify I1 (the watch record on end) in the player progress hooks.
I did not check whether another control on the collection list (e.g. ChromeButtons' DriveTreeToggle) shares the same toggle path.
trajectory: Each r7 fix round adds a new piece of state or a new branch to patch something the earlier rounds introduced. 0a1ba745 adds a `replacesTrail` flag to QueuePageState, splitting the queue-page trail override added earlier. 16ac5ada adds a `visitUntilLeft` prop and two refs (visitRoute, visitStarted) to the treeVisitStore visit logic added earlier, and that new state introduces F1: the toggle's filePage branch never anticipated a visit with no file. bc6be1f1 adds a `sidebarOverlay` field to LeftPaneState to gate the `extraRowWidth` adjustment added in the previous round. Only 5fe9be41 removes a branch (`onSelect` is no longer conditional on fileId). The tree-pane visibility logic is being patched: visit, yield, narrow-open and filePage are now four interacting stores/flags, and the latest fix produced a new breach where two of them meet.
